html:
On 24 September 1853 a French admiral took possession of New Caledonia at Balade, on its northeast coast, for the emperor Napoleon III.

James Cook had named the island in 1774, and Protestant and Catholic missionaries had followed. France wanted a naval base and a place for convicts, and it moved before Britain could. Nouméa was founded in 1854.

The Kanak, the island's Melanesian people, were pushed into reserves as land went to settlers and to the penal colony. This led to the revolt of 1878 and, a century later, to the independence struggle led by Jean-Marie Tjibaou.
sum: On 24 September 1853 a French admiral took possession of New Caledonia at Balade, on its northeast coast, for the emperor Napoleon III.
